evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Delivery › Can I schedule an order for later?
evidence.content: Not yet — orders go straight to the kitchen when placed.

evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Ordering › How do I place an order?
evidence.content:
Three ways, all against the same menu and account:

1. **Website** — browse the menu, add to cart, and check out.
2. **Telegram** — chat with the DosaDash bot; link it to your account once
   and order by message (voice notes arrive in a later release).
3. **AI assistant** — ask in plain language ("2 masala dosas and a filter
   coffee"); the assistant builds an order draft you confirm before anything
   is placed. Nothing is ever ordered without your explicit confirmation.

evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Ordering › What are your hours?
evidence.content:
Kitchen hours are set by the restaurant and shown on the site. Outside
hours, or when the kitchen is temporarily paused, checkout is disabled and
the assistant will say so rather than take an order it can't fulfil.

evidence.heading: Ordering, Cancellation & Refund Policies › Cancellation policy
evidence.content:
- You may cancel an order yourself **only while it is in PLACED status** —
  i.e. before the kitchen confirms it. Use the order page or ask support.
- Once an order is CONFIRMED or COOKING, self-service cancellation is no
  longer possible (ingredients are committed). Contact support; staff can
  cancel at their discretion before the order is READY.
- Orders that are READY, OUT FOR DELIVERY, or DELIVERED cannot be cancelled.

evidence.heading: Ordering, Cancellation & Refund Policies › Hours & kitchen availability
evidence.content:
- Orders are accepted only within the kitchen's configured business hours;
  the restaurant may also pause the kitchen temporarily (rush, maintenance).
  While closed or paused, no channel — web, Telegram, or AI assistant — will
  accept an order.
- Individual dishes may have their own serving windows (e.g. breakfast-only
  items) and may sell out during the day.

evidence.heading: Frequently Asked Questions › Ordering › Can I customise a dish?
evidence.content:
Spice level can be adjusted on most cooked-to-order dishes (dosas, curries,
biryanis) — mention it in the item notes. Common requests: "less spicy",
"no onion", "chutney/masala packed separately", "ghee on the side".

evidence.heading: Rice, Pongal & Biryani Guide › Biryani › Mutton Biryani — ₹280
evidence.content:
Slow-cooked mutton, richest and heaviest of the biryanis. Contains dairy
(curd). 35-minute prep — worth it.

evidence.heading: Allergen & Dietary Guide › Biryani

| Mutton Biryani | non-veg | no | medium | dairy |

| Veg Biryani | veg | no | medium | dairy |

evidence.heading: Rice, Pongal & Biryani Guide › Biryani › Veg Biryani — ₹180
evidence.content:
Seasonal vegetables on basmati (the one biryani NOT on seeraga samba), with
mint raita. Contains dairy (curd). Vegetarian but not vegan and not
Jain-friendly (contains onion).

evidence.heading: Rice, Pongal & Biryani Guide › Rice & Pongal › Curd Rice — ₹100
evidence.content:
Cooling curd rice with a mustard-curry leaf tempering and pomegranate.
Contains dairy and mustard. Jain-friendly, no spice. The traditional last
course — and the best order for an upset stomach or a hot afternoon.

evidence.heading: Rice, Pongal & Biryani Guide › Biryani › Chicken Biryani — ₹220
evidence.content:
The flagship. Seeraga samba rice, curd marinade, Chettinad masala. Contains
dairy (curd).

evidence.heading: Chettinad Curries, Snacks, Sweets & Beverages Guide › Chettinad Curries › Pepper Mutton — ₹290
evidence.content:
Dry-roasted mutton tossed in cracked black pepper and curry leaves. Hot.
A dry preparation (not a gravy) — great as a side to Sambar Rice.
